accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS ELA L.1.1h ('Use determiners, e.g., articles, demonstratives'), the National Curriculum in England English Appendix 2 (Year 3: 'use of the forms a or an according to whether the next word begins with a consonant or a vowel, e.g. a rock, an open box'; Year 4 terminology: determiner) and Cambridge Grammar of English on a/an by sound (an hour, a unicorn, a uniform, a one-way street). Demonstratives: this/these near the speaker, that/those far; this/that singular, these/those plural. The adult text first said a/an was Year 1-2 and was corrected to Year 3/Year 4 before commit.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early errors: choosing a/an by spelling rather than sound (an unicorn, a hour: step 2 prediction, challenge tag letter, m2), 'a apple' before the rule is heard (step 1 prediction, tag sound), singular demonstrative with a plural noun (this shoes, that birds: tags one/many, m5), near/far swaps (tags near/far, step 4 prediction) and using a for an already-known referent (I saw a dog. A dog barked: tag again, p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagthis is built on a near mat / far shelf scene with a child at the left: objects appear near or far, one or many, and the learner taps this/that/these/those in a 2 x 2 grid (near-far by one-many), after a/an chosen by the highlighted first sound and a/the by known vs any. flagdetpro (412, Year 4 grammar terms, determiner vs pronoun) and flagpfx/flagwfam are different mechanisms; the gate measured under 30% shingle overlap.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule is met by doing before it is stated: the first letter of each word is coloured so the learner listens to it; hour and unicorn break the letter rule and the feedback spells out the sound ('our: the h is silent'); the dashed pointing line runs to the near mat or far shelf so distance is seen; the 2 x 2 grid labels each box 'near, many' etc., and wrong taps say which of the two checks failed.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: 'a egg' (step 1), 'an unicorn' because unicorn starts with u (step 2, the tasks then show 'a unicorn' by sound) and 'Look at this kite!' for a far-away kite (step 4). The completion messages echo the locked-in choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, two wrong options each with their own message: 'these and those are for many things. Here there is only one', 'Hour starts with the letter h, but the h is silent...', 'Check where they are. Near me is this or these...', 'We already know which cat...'. In-lab slips name which check failed: 'There are 3 shells. Many needs these, not this' vs 'Look where they are: far away, so those'.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes; kid paragraphs grade 1.3, adult 7.1. In the lab every prompt is one short line ('Say it out loud. Listen to the first sound.'), answer pads are single words at 28-30 px, and the young class gives 56 px buttons.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each step has one job (a/an, tricky sounds, a/the, this/that, these/those) and every feedback line names the word and the reason.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every step before and after Show me: the two answer pads and the 2 x 2 grid fill the width as large tap targets, near objects sit on the mat clear of the child figure (moved from 0.28W to 0.38W after the first screenshots showed overlap), and the feedback strip fits.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a matching button in the Lab buttons group (a, an, the, this, that, these, those) with aria-labels; the canvas aria-label and c.say live text read the current word, where the object is and how many ('3 shells are near you. Pick this, these, that or those.'). Walkthrough and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) pass in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.

sources: Department for Education (2013) National Curriculum in England: English Appendix 2, Vocabulary, grammar and punctuation (Year 3 a/an; Year 4 determiner)
Carter & McCarthy, Cambridge Grammar of English (2006), articles and demonstratives
Oxford Learner's Dictionaries usage note: a or an before vowel sounds (an hour, a university)
